landing.title: How testee works
landing.text: testee turns your job description into a timed interview, with its own random questions for every candidate. This page walks through it, from creating an interview to sharing the results.
actions: Paste the job description in the box at the top, or pick a ready template; adjust the topics, and the questions are written and checked for you.
Invite candidates by email, from a file, with a share link in your job ad, or from your ATS, your own platform or an AI assistant.
See what candidates see: a timed interview in your brand, answered with a click or by voice.
Read the reports: every candidate's answers, grades and integrity signals, shared by email or chat in a click.
Connect your ATS, your platform and AI apps, get updates in Slack, or ask Mira, the AI assistant, to do the work for you.
Compare testee with phone screens and subscriptions, and see how questions are checked and improved.
tips: Creating interviews is free. You pay per candidate who answers, at the prices further down the page, in your currency, and your first candidates are free.
Try your interview as a candidate before you invite anyone.
Watch the video from the button at the top for a short tour; the FAQ and the guides are at the bottom of the page.
Download the report samples under the reports to see what real reports look like.

companies.title: Companies
companies.text: Your companies. Everything you do in testee happens inside one: its interviews, candidates, team, credits and integrations.
actions: Create a company with “new company”. Its name is unique across testee.
Open a company to work on its interviews and candidates.
Remove a company you own, with all its interviews and invites; its credits are lost and aren't refunded.
Open a company's ⋮ menu for its team; owners and admins also top up and open its brand and billing there.
tips: Your role shows beside each company you don't own: admins change things; viewers mostly look, and can also write notes, rate and report questions, try interviews and share reports.
Credits belong to a company, so each one tops up on its own.

pickCompany.title: Choose a company
pickCompany.text: You picked a template. Choose the company it's for: the template is copied there as a new interview, free and ready to send to candidates.
actions: Pick a company to open the template in it, then use it.
Create a new company if you don't have one yet; the template opens there.
tips: Once copied, the interview is the company's own: change its questions and settings as you like.
Only owners and admins can use a template; in a company where you're a viewer, the button isn't there.

interviews.title: Interviews
interviews.text: All of this company's interviews and its credits for candidates. Each interview is a timed test made from a job description or a template.
actions: Create an interview from a job description with “new interview” (owners and admins).
Open an interview to see its topics, candidates and notes, its settings (owners and admins) and, once the company has topped up, Discover; a pinned note shows under its name.
Search the interviews by title, or filter them by status: new, in process or hired.
Try an interview as a candidate from its ⋮ menu; owners and admins can also delete it there.
Top up credits from the balance, or turn on automatic top-ups on the Billing tab (owners and admins).
tips: The balance turns amber when credits run low. Without credits, new invites aren't sent.
The company's menu leads to templates, your team, integrations, brand and billing (owners and admins), the action log (the owner) and referrals.

newInterview.title: New interview
newInterview.text: Start an interview from the job description. testee reads it, proposes the topics to test, and writes the questions once you approve them.
actions: Paste the job description: the role, its requirements and nice-to-haves.
With nothing typed yet, “try an example” fills the box with a sample description.
Choose the language to generate the interview in.
Generate, then review the proposed topics.
Start from a template instead, or from a job in your ATS once one is connected.
Started from the home page, choose the company it's for, or create one; only companies you own or admin are listed.
tips: The more specific the description, the closer the questions fit the role.
Generating is free: you pay only for candidates who answer.
A company can hold only a few interviews with no candidates yet and start only a few a day; the limits are higher once it has topped up.

reviewTopics.title: Review your topics
reviewTopics.text: testee proposed these topics from your description. Each topic you keep gets its own set of questions with answers.
actions: Uncheck the topics you don't need.
Edit a topic's name and subtopics with its pencil.
Add a topic of your own with “add a topic”: give it a name and at least 3 subtopics.
Describe changes in your own words and apply them, for example “add a topic on team leadership”.
Approve and generate to write the questions.
Cancel to drop the interview; nothing generated so far is kept.
tips: With too many topics, uncheck some or describe how to merge them.
Questions are written only after you approve, so take a minute here.
A review left open for 14 days is cancelled, and its interview removed.

generating.title: Generating
generating.text: testee is making your interview: first the topics, then the questions for each one. It takes a few minutes.
actions: Leave this page if you like: generation keeps going.
Cancel the generation if you no longer need it; nothing made so far is kept.
Once the topics are ready, this page shows them for your review; questions are written only after you approve.
If generation fails, select Retry, or Start over.
tips: You get a notification when the interview is ready.
Once the company has topped up, an interview made through the API skips the review: its questions are written from the proposed topics.
Come back any time from the interviews list.

interviewTopics.title: Topics
interviewTopics.text: What this interview tests: its topics, each with subtopics and its own pool of questions. Every candidate gets a random set from each pool.
actions: Open a topic to go to its questions: read them, like, dislike or report them, and, as an owner or admin, disable some.
Re-generate a weak question or mark a wrong answer on a topic's questions page (owners and admins).

Set how many questions each candidate gets from a topic (owners and admins); 0 leaves the topic out for new candidates, but at least one topic must keep questions. A candidate gets at most 60 questions over all topics: lower one topic to raise another.
Try the interview as a candidate from the ⋮ menu; owners and admins can also delete it there.
tips: AI-written questions can be wrong, even though a second AI checks a sample of answers: skim each topic before you invite anyone.
Click the title to rename the interview (owners and admins).
The cards at the top add up what each candidate gets: the total questions, the average time per question and the whole interview's time. They follow every change.

topicQuestions.title: Questions
topicQuestions.text: One topic's questions with their answers, likes, dislikes and reports. Every candidate gets a random set from the active ones.
actions: See how many questions there are, how many are active or disabled and how many reports they have in the cards at the top; filter the list by All, Active, Disabled or Reported.
Untick a question to disable it: no candidate gets it from now on. Tick it to make it active again (owners and admins).
Like or dislike a question; click your choice again to take it back.
Open a question's reports and add your own, once per question.
Re-generate a weak question or mark a wrong answer from its ⋮ menu (owners and admins); a marked answer is checked, then fixed or replaced if it's wrong.
tips: AI-written questions can be wrong: read them before you invite anyone.
Your likes, dislikes and reports count the same as candidates' and help fix weak questions.
The topic's count is of active questions only: a candidate never gets more from it than that.

interviewCandidates.title: Candidates
interviewCandidates.text: Everyone invited to this interview, with their status, progress and grade.
actions: Invite candidates with “new candidate(s)” (owners and admins): one at a time, a list, or a CSV or TXT file.
Search by email or name, filter by status, and sort by grade or date.
Open a candidate's report, or download or share the report on all candidates.
Open a candidate's ⋮ menu to resend the invite, copy its link, revoke it or delete the candidate (owners and admins).
tips: Each candidate who answers at least one question uses credits, including those from the link.
A candidate who hasn't started gets one reminder 3 days after the invite. An invite not started within 30 days expires; resending it makes it work again.
Candidates take it in the interview's mode; to change one candidate's, use their page. A candidate in another mode than the interview's shows that mode's icon.
Inviting sets a candidate's credits aside; they're given back if the candidate finishes without answering.
Candidates from the shareable link, your ATS, the API or Discover show here too.
The report on all candidates is shared as a PDF by email, or as a short summary by WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or LINE.

interviewNotes.title: Notes
interviewNotes.text: Your team's notes on this hiring round: what you agreed, whom to call next, or whom the interview is for. Everyone in your company, viewers included, sees them and can write them; candidates never do.
actions: Write a note in the box at the top and select Post, or press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter. Links in it become clickable.
Edit or delete your own notes from the ⋮ menu on their row; owners and admins can delete anyone's.
Pin a note with “pin to the top” in its ⋮ menu (owners and admins): one note at a time shows first here, and under the interview's name on its page and in the interviews list.
tips: Working for clients? Pin a note like “For Acme, Backend Developer” to see at a glance whom each interview is for.
A deleted note is gone for good. The action log records who wrote, changed, deleted or pinned a note, never its text.
The rest of your team hears of each new note: in the bell, in the daily activity digest and, with Slack connected, in your channel.

interviewDiscover.title: Discover
interviewDiscover.text: People who practise on testee and chose to be open to offers, whose practice covers this interview's subjects at its level. Each shows their name, LinkedIn profile and latest practice result on each matching subject. Only companies that have topped up at least once see this tab.
actions: Open someone's LinkedIn profile to learn more about them.
Invite someone to this interview (owners and admins): it goes to their account's email and costs credits like any invite.
tips: These are practice results, not a qualification, and the list is not a recommendation: whoever practised last comes first.
Someone who turns Open to offers off disappears from this list at once.

interviewSettings.title: Settings
interviewSettings.text: How this interview runs for every candidate. Only owners and admins see this tab.
actions: Turn on the shareable link for a job ad: anyone with it can take the interview, and each person who answers through it uses credits like an invited candidate.

Choose the interview mode: click mode, where candidates tap their answers, or voice mode, where Mira, an AI interviewer, reads each question aloud and candidates answer by voice or tap. Voice mode works in every language; how well it reads and hears varies by language, and the link under the setting opens the guide with the quality in each.
Set the average time per question, in seconds: each question gets its own time from its length and any code it shows, and the interview's total time stays the same.
Set the passing grade: candidates who reach it pass.
Mark the interview as hired once you've filled the role.
Keep the interview's questions out of testee's shared question bank; questions already reused in other interviews stay there.
tips: Number fields save as soon as you leave them; switches and the mode save at once.
The interview never shows candidates their score or whether an answer was right; only their own data download has their grade.
For one candidate who needs more time, add extra time on their page.
A new mode applies to candidates who haven't started, except those given their own on their page.
The average time is 10 to 600 seconds; the passing grade is 1 to 100%.

tryInterview.title: Try as a candidate
tryInterview.text: A preview of this interview just as candidates see it: the intro, then the timed questions. It's free.
actions: Tick the pledge, select “accept & start”, and answer as a candidate would.
Check the timing, the wording and the answers before you invite anyone.
tips: Stay on the page while you answer: for candidates, leaving the page, copying and answering too fast are recorded.
A voice mode interview first asks for your microphone and sound: allow them, and Mira reads each question aloud while you answer by voice or tap.
Each company has a number of previews a day, fewer in voice mode; once they're used up, starting one says when you can try again.
A preview stays out of the candidates list and the questions' statistics.
Viewers can try an interview too.

candidate.title: Candidate report
candidate.text: One candidate's results: their grade, whether they passed, and each topic's score with every answer.
actions: Read each answer, with integrity flags: page leaves, copy attempts and fast answers.
Once they finish, see any unusual patterns in their answers and times, and questions they got right to ask about in a live interview.
Download the report as a PDF, or share it: the PDF by email, or a short summary by WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or LINE. Viewers can email it only to the company's members.
Give +25%, +50% or +100% extra time before they start, for example for a disability.
Choose whether they take it by click or by voice, whatever the interview's mode, until they start.
Add or edit the candidate's name.
Copy their invite link to send it yourself, if the email didn't arrive; it's there until they finish or the invite expires.
Resend or revoke the invite, or delete the candidate with their results.
tips: The score supports your decision; it doesn't make it. If the candidate asks, have a person review their result.
A check mark under the grade shows the candidate confirmed, before starting, that they'd answer on their own, without AI tools or other people.

A grade is the percentage of points earned: each question is worth one point, and a "pick multiple options" question earns part of it for each right option ticked, and nothing if a wrong one is ticked.
Extra time, the candidate's mode and name, the invite link, resending, revoking and deleting are for owners and admins.

templates.title: Templates
templates.text: Ready-made interviews for common roles. Using one copies it into this company as your own interview.
actions: Search by role or topic, and filter by level and language.
Open a template to see its topics and how many questions each has.
See on each row its topics, questions and minutes, and how many of your interviews used it.
Use a template to start an interview from it (owners and admins).
tips: For a closer fit, create an interview from your own job description instead.
Once copied, the interview is yours: change its questions and settings as you like.
The list starts with your language and English; choose all languages to see the rest.

template.title: Template
template.text: A ready-made interview: its topics, their subtopics and how many questions each topic has.
actions: Check that the topics match the role you're hiring for.
Use the template to copy it into this company as a new interview (owners and admins).
tips: Copying is free; candidates who answer use credits as usual.
If the topics don't fit, create an interview from your job description instead.
Its questions stay hidden until you use it.

team.title: Team
team.text: The people who work on this company's interviews, and their roles.
actions: Add a member by email, as an admin or a viewer: they're emailed a link to join.
Change a member's role between admin and viewer.
Hand the company to an admin who has joined, with “make owner” in their menu: you become an admin.
Copy a pending invite's link, or remove a member or an invite.
tips: Admins create and change interviews, invite candidates and top up. Viewers see interviews and results, share reports and write notes, but change nothing else.
Removing a member whose card pays for automatic top-ups, or making them a viewer, stops those top-ups.
Only the owner adds, changes and removes members; everyone in the company sees the team.

actions.title: Action log
actions.text: Everything the company's members did, newest first: what they did and to what, who did it, when, and whether the AI assistant, an AI app, the API or an ATS did it for them. Only the owner sees it.
actions: Show one member's actions, or one kind: interviews, candidates, team, company, billing or integrations.
Show the actions between two days.
Download the log as a CSV file from the ⋮ menu: all time, a recent period or between two days. Up to 20 downloads a company a day.

Download a bias-audit export: a CSV file of every candidate who finished with a grade, for all interviews or one and, if you like, between two days, with their grade, the passing grade, whether they passed and whether they scored above the interview's median, keyed by email.
tips: Actions are kept for 12 months.
People aren't kept in the log: a deleted candidate shows as such, and a member who left as a former member.
An API key's actions show under the key's name, and a deleted key's as a deleted key's.
A member's views of one candidate's results show once a day, at the latest view.

testee holds no data on sex, race or ethnicity: add your candidates' own self-reported answers by email, then remove the email column before you share the file with your independent auditor, for a New York City bias audit (Local Law 144) or the EEOC's four-fifths rule. Up to 20 exports a company a day, and each shows in the log.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.text: Connect testee to the tools your team already uses. Each integration opens its own page with setup steps.
actions: Slack: get your company's notifications in a channel.
API: keys, web hooks and the SDK to connect your own platform.
AI apps: use testee from Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps.
ATS (Workable, Greenhouse, Teamtailor, Recruitee, Breezy HR): candidates you move to a stage get the interview, and their results go back.
tips: Everyone in the company sees the integrations; owners and admins change them. AI apps are each person's own: anyone can connect or disconnect theirs.

ats.title: ATS integration
ats.text: Link a job in your ATS to an interview: candidates you move into a chosen stage get the interview, and their results come back as a comment on their profile.
actions: Connect your ATS by following its instructions.
Link a job: choose the job, its stage and an interview, or make a new interview from the job's text.
See how many candidates each linked job invited, has waiting or couldn't invite.
Invite again candidates who weren't invited, for example when credits ran out.
Reconnect when the ATS stops working: candidates aren't invited until you do.
Unlink a job, or disconnect the ATS.
tips: Add a stage just for testee, like “testee skills test”, so it never mixes with your other tools.
testee never moves or rejects anyone in your ATS.
If the member who connected the ATS leaves or becomes a viewer, candidates stop being invited.

slack.title: Slack
slack.text: Your company's notifications in a Slack channel, as they happen.
actions: Add testee to Slack and pick the channel, for example #hiring.
Choose which notifications go there: a candidate finishing, an invite that wasn't delivered, an interview being ready and more.
Send a test message to the channel, and reconnect if Slack stops taking messages.
Disconnect to stop them and remove testee's app from your Slack.
tips: testee can only post to that channel; it can't read your Slack.
The bell still shows everyone their notifications, with billing ones for owners and admins only.
If the member who connected Slack leaves or becomes a viewer, it stops until an owner or admin reconnects it.

api.title: API
api.text: Connect your own platform, such as your careers site, to testee.
actions: Create an API key and tick only what it needs: reading or creating interviews; reading, inviting, changing or removing candidates; reading or adding notes; reading your credits; or use with AI agents (MCP). It acts for the company as itself, and keeps working when the person who made it leaves.
Open a key to change what it may do, each change saved at once, and the IP addresses it may be used from.
Rename a key, create a replacement when it's about to expire, and, as the owner, see what it did.
Add a web hook: testee tells your HTTPS address, signed, when a candidate starts, finishes (with their results), isn't reached, expires or is removed, and when an interview is ready.
Send a web hook a test event, and see what each send got in its delivery log.
Roll a web hook's secret: for 24 hours both secrets sign each request.
On the SDK tab, list the sites that may show your interviews with the SDK, and allow localhost while you test.
Delete the keys and web hooks you no longer use.
Open the developer docs for every endpoint and event, and the SDK.
tips: A new key and a web hook's secret show only once: copy them right away.
Choose an expiry for each key: a leaked key that never expires stays usable.
You can tick or untick a key's permissions later; give each key only what its platform needs.
A web hook that doesn't answer for 3 days is paused; a test event that goes through starts it again.

aiApps.title: AI apps
aiApps.text: Use testee from your AI chat: ask Claude or ChatGPT about your interviews and candidates, or to make changes for you.
actions: Copy the server address and add it to Claude, Claude Code or ChatGPT, following the steps; the developer docs cover other apps and your own agents.
Allow the app on the testee page that opens.
Once an app is connected, copy an example of what to ask it.
Disconnect an app you no longer use.
Owners and admins allow or stop AI apps in this company: while they're off, apps can't read or change anything in it.
tips: An app acts as you, in every company you're in that allows AI apps. Most apps ask you before they change anything.
It can't see your password or API keys, and can't delete your account or a company.

referrals.title: Referrals
referrals.text: Invite other companies to testee with this company's link, and you both earn credits.
actions: Copy your referral link to share it.
See the companies that came through your link and topped up, the credits each one gave you, and how many rewards are left this year.
tips: You both get credits when the company you invited makes its first top-up, of any amount.
Credits go to this company and never expire.
Each side gets 1,000 credits. Your company earns this up to 25 times a year; past that, the company you invited still gets its credits.
A top-up that's refunded, by any amount, or charged back in full takes both rewards back.

brand.title: Brand
brand.text: Your logo, colors, fonts and rounding on your candidates' invitation, interview and finished page. The logo also shows in their emails.
actions: Set, change or remove the logo.
Pick the fonts for titles and for text, and how round the cards and buttons are.
Pick the colors of each group, one set for the light theme and one for the dark, and see them in the preview.
Save them, undo unsaved changes with “reset”, or go back to testee's colors, fonts and rounding with “reset to testee defaults”.
tips: Colors whose text would be hard to read can't be saved, so every candidate can read the questions.
Members trying an interview see it in your colors too.
Only owners and admins see this page.

billing.title: Billing
billing.text: Where this company's credits came from and where they went.
actions: Top up, or set up automatic top-ups.
See the candidates whose credits are reserved.
Open the invoice of any top-up.
Narrow the history to top-ups, charges or refunds, or download it as a CSV file. Up to 20 downloads a company a day.
tips: A candidate's credits are reserved when they're invited, charged once they answer, and given back if they don't.
Only owners and admins see this page.

You can refund credits you bought in the last 14 days and haven't spent from the top-up's row in the history, through Paddle or by writing to us. Credits reserved for candidates can't be refunded while reserved.

topUp.title: Top up
topUp.text: Buy credits for any company you belong to as an owner or admin.
actions: Pick a company, then type how many candidates to top up, from 10 to 1,000, or pick a price step: larger top-ups cost less per candidate.
Change the company's currency at the top of the page: its top-ups, automatic ones too, are priced and charged in it from then on.
Pay in Paddle's checkout; the credits arrive within seconds.
Open pricing to compare the top-ups.
Set up automatic top-up: choose an amount and a balance, and tick the agreement. Your card is saved in Paddle's checkout and charged each time the balance falls under that level.
tips: A candidate costs 500 credits: reserved when they're invited, charged once they answer, and given back if they don't.
Credits never expire. Each top-up's invoice is on the company's billing tab.
Prices don't include VAT or sales tax: where it applies, it's added at checkout.
You can refund credits you bought in the last 14 days and haven't spent on the company's billing page, through Paddle or by writing to us.
Owners and admins set up automatic top-up. Only the person whose card pays can change it or update the card; any owner or admin can turn it off at once.
A declined card is tried again after 1, 3 and 7 days, then automatic top-up pauses until the card is updated. A card that can't pay, such as an expired one, pauses it at once.

settings.title: Settings
settings.text: Your own account: the language testee speaks to you, your currency, the emails you get, and your data.
actions: Choose the language of the site, the AI assistant's replies and your emails; new interviews start in it too.
Choose the currency prices show in, wherever you are. A company's top-ups are in the company's own currency, set on its top-up page.
Choose which optional emails you get; service emails, such as invites, reports and billing problems, always go out.
Turn Open to offers on or off: while it's on, companies hiring on testee for the subjects you practised see your name, LinkedIn profile and practice results, and may invite you.
Download everything testee holds about you, or delete your account.
Copy your account ID to quote when you write to us.
tips: Deleting your account deletes the companies only you are in, and their credits aren't refunded. A company others have joined needs another owner first, or must be deleted.
Open to offers needs your LinkedIn profile, and turns itself off a year after you last turned it on.

join.title: Company invite
join.text: You were invited to join a company's team on testee, to work on its interviews and candidates.
actions: Sign in with the email the invitation was sent to.
Join the company: it then appears in your companies.
Open the company if you've already joined it.
tips: Signed in with another email? Sign out and sign in with the invited one; the invite only works for it.
Your role, admin or viewer, is the one the person who invited you chose.
An invite that was already used, or that the owner removed, no longer works.

connect.title: Connect an AI app
connect.text: An AI app asks to use your testee account. Here you choose whether it may.
actions: Sign in, if you aren't yet, to see which app is asking.
Read what the app can and can't do with your account.
Turn off “allow changes” to let the app only read.
Allow the app, or deny it; either way you go back to the app.
tips: When testee doesn't know the app, allow it only if you started connecting it yourself.
Disconnect an app any time in a company's Integrations, under AI apps.
A link that has expired or was already used no longer works: start connecting again from your AI app.

news.title: News
news.text: What's new at testee: new features, improvements and updates, newest first.
actions: Scroll down to read older news.
Follow the news in your feed reader with the RSS link at the top.
tips: News shows in your notifications; the major ones also come by email while “product updates and news” is on in your settings.

practice.title: Free practice
practice.text: Free timed practice interviews for common roles, for anyone preparing for a job interview.
actions: Search by role or topic, and filter by level and language.
Open a practice interview to see its topics and start it.
tips: Until you choose languages, the list shows your site language and English.
Practice is private: no company sees your results unless you turn on Open to offers.
Signed in, a check after a title marks a practice you've started, and a double check one you've finished; hover the check to see how many topics you've completed.

practiceTest.title: Practice interview
practiceTest.text: One free practice interview: its level, language, length and the topics it covers.
actions: Choose the time per question before you start: the standard time, double, or no time limit.
Start a practice round; sign in first if you aren't yet.
See how far your latest round got on each topic.
Signed in, open your past rounds with “your rounds” beside “start practice”.
Hiring for this role? Create an interview from it for your own candidates.
tips: Each round is timed unless you choose no time limit; once done, you see your grade and every right answer.
Practise as often as you like, within an hourly limit on new rounds: it's free.

practiceHistory.title: Your rounds
practiceHistory.text: Every round you've taken of this practice interview, newest first, with its progress and grade.
actions: Open a round to see its results and every answer.
Practise again to start a new round.
tips: Compare your grades over time to see where you're improving.

practiceRound.title: Practice results
practiceRound.text: One practice round's results: your grade, each topic's score, and every question with its right answers and your picks; a "pick multiple options" question also shows the points it earned.
actions: Read each question, its right answers and what you picked.
Rate a question, or report it if its answer is wrong; reported questions get checked and fixed.
Continue a round you haven't finished.
Practise again, or open your past rounds.
tips: Whatever you picked when a question's time runs out still counts; a question left with nothing picked, or never reached, counts as wrong.
Hiring for this role? Create an interview from it for your own candidates.

Looking for a job? After a finished round, enter your LinkedIn profile and turn on Open to offers to let companies hiring for these subjects see your name, profile and latest practice results and invite you; it stays on for a year unless you turn it off.

features.title: Features
features.text: Everything testee does for a company, from a job description to a hire: creating interviews, inviting candidates, what candidates see, reports, integrations, compliance and pricing.
actions: Jump to the box at the end of the page with “create an interview” at the top, or open pricing.
Jump to a group with the tabs at the top: create, invite, interview, decide, connect, trust and pricing.
See the main features beside a picture of the real app, and the others as cards under them.
Paste a job description in the box at the end of the page to create an interview.
Open the pricing page, the developer docs or the trust page from their groups.
Ask Mira, or open the FAQ or the guides, at the end of the page.
tips: Every feature is included: you pay only for each candidate who answers at least one question.

hiringFlow.title: Hiring flow
hiringFlow.text: Every step of hiring with testee, from the job description you paste to the report you share and the hire you make, with every option at each step.
actions: Scroll down the line: each step shows what happens, its options and a picture of the real app.
See the ways candidates can come in and the ways reports can go out, under the invite and share steps.
Jump to the start box with “create an interview” at the top, or open all features.
Paste a job description in the box at the end of the page to start.
Ask Mira, or open the FAQ or the guides, at the end of the page.
tips: Creating interviews is free: you pay only for each candidate who answers at least one question.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.text: What testee costs: generating interviews is free, and you pay per candidate who answers, with no subscription.
actions: See today's price per candidate, and the lower prices for larger top-ups.
See how many first candidates are free.
See how many credits a candidate takes; tax is added at checkout where it applies.
See the credits you earn by inviting another company.
Top up a company's credits.
tips: Credits never expire.
A candidate who doesn't answer any question costs nothing.
Unused paid credits can be refunded within 14 days, on the company's billing page.

tests.title: Skills tests by role
tests.text: Ready-made timed skills tests for common roles, to use as they are or as a start.
actions: Search by role or topic, and filter by level and language.
Open a test to see what it checks, with sample questions.
tips: Until you choose languages, the list shows your site language and English.
For a closer fit, create a test from your own job description on the home page.

test.title: Role skills test
test.text: A ready-made timed skills test for one role: what it checks, sample questions, and how to use it with your candidates.
actions: See the topics and subtopics it tests.
Read sample questions with their right answers.
Create a test for your candidates from your job description.
Practise it yourself for free, as a candidate would.
Read answers to the questions companies ask before testing candidates.
tips: Your candidates get their own random questions, never the samples shown here.

compare.title: Compare testee
compare.text: Sourced comparisons of testee with other pre-employment testing tools: how tests are made, what they cost and when each fits better.
actions: Open a comparison to read it.
Create a test for your candidates from the card at the end.
tips: Each comparison shows when it was last updated.

comparison.title: Comparison
comparison.text: How testee compares with other tools on one question: how tests are made, what they cost and when each one fits better.
actions: Read the comparison and follow its links to the sources.
Jump to a section from the “on this page” list, on longer pages.
Create a test for your candidates from the button at the top or the card at the end.
Go back to every comparison with the back arrow by the title.
tips: Prices and features change: the date under the title shows when the page was last updated.

guides.title: Guides for hiring
guides.text: Practical guides for hiring managers: screening applicants, skills tests, and using AI in hiring fairly and legally.
actions: Search the guides.
Open a guide to read it.
tips: Each guide shows when it was last updated.

guide.title: Guide
guide.text: A practical guide for hiring managers on one topic.
actions: Read the guide and follow its links to sources and related pages.
Jump to a section from the “on this page” list, on longer pages.
Create a test for your candidates from the button at the top or the card at the end.
Go back to every guide with the back arrow by the title.
tips: Legal topics are dated summaries, not legal advice: check the rules that apply where you hire.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.text: Answers to common questions about testee: interviews, candidates, prices and credits, results, integrations, languages and your data.
actions: Jump to a group of questions with the buttons at the top.
Click a question to open its answer.
tips: Didn't find your answer? Ask Mira, the AI assistant, or write to us, from the card at the end of the page.
Prices in the answers are always today's.

about.title: About us
about.text: Who makes testee and why: interviews made from a job description that any team can afford, and free practice for anyone.
actions: Read why testee exists and how it approaches hiring.
Read a word from the founder, and open his LinkedIn profile.
Create a test, or practise for free, from the card at the end.
tips: To write to the team, use the contact page.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.text: Write to the testee team with a question, an idea, a partnership offer or something that isn't working.
actions: Fill in your name, your email and your message, then send it.
Paste the ID of the company, interview, candidate or account it's about into your message, so we find it at once.
See who runs testee: company name, registry code, address and email.
tips: The “copy id” link is under a company's, an interview's or a candidate's name; your account's ID is in your account menu.
We reply to the email you give.

apiDocs.title: Developer docs
apiDocs.text: Everything you need to connect your own platform or AI agent to testee, read from the API itself so it always matches it.
actions: API: how to sign in, guides such as rate limits and safe retries, the base URL, every endpoint with its parameters, body, response and errors, the error list and the changelog.
Web hooks: the events testee sends to your address and what each one carries.
SDK: how to embed the interview on your own site.
MCP: how to connect an AI app or your own agent, and the tools it gets.
Objects: every object the API returns, field by field.
tips: Create API keys and web hooks in a company's Integrations, under API.
The docs are in English only.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.text: How testee works for people with disabilities, what still falls short, and how to tell us.
actions: See what testee does for accessibility, such as themes, phone layouts and keyboard use.
See what falls short, such as timed questions.
Write to us by email if something is hard to use or you need it in another form.
tips: Taking a company's interview and need more time? Ask the company for extra time before you start; you don't have to say why.
We answer within 14 days; if you aren't satisfied, you can contact the Estonian Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (TTJA).

documents.title: Legal docs
documents.text: Documents for companies that assess candidates with testee: instructions, templates and the data processing agreement.
actions: Download the instructions for companies: what a grade means, human review, passing grades and extra time.
Download editable notice templates to send candidates before you invite them.
Download the DPIA template, with testee's part filled in, to complete.
Download the data processing agreement, or read it online.
tips: The documents are in English only.

trust.title: Trust and security
trust.text: How testee keeps your data and your candidates' data safe: security, privacy, compliance with the hiring laws, where data is stored, who processes it and how long it is kept.
actions: See how testee protects data: sign-in, encryption, access checks, rate limits and backups.
See what testee provides for the GDPR, the EU AI Act, the UK and the US, New York City's bias-audit law included.
See where data is stored, the sub-processors that handle it and how long each kind of data is kept.
Open the terms, the privacy policy, the data processing agreement and the documents for companies.
Open the accessibility statement.
tips: For a question about security, privacy or compliance, or to report a security problem, write to the email at the end of the page.

terms.title: Terms
terms.text: The terms for using testee: accounts, companies, credits and payments, tests for candidates, acceptable use and liability.
actions: Read the version in force, with the day it applies from.
Open an earlier or upcoming version from the list of versions at the end.
Switch to the English text when you read a translation.
tips: Only the English text is binding.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: How testee collects, uses and protects the personal data of companies, their members and candidates, and the rights you have.
actions: Read the version in force, with the day it applies from.
Open an earlier or upcoming version from the list of versions at the end.
Switch to the English text when you read a translation.
tips: Only the English text is binding.
To get a copy of your data or delete your account, open your settings.

dpa.title: Data processing agreement
dpa.text: The agreement between testee and companies that test candidates: what testee processes on your behalf and how.
actions: Read the version in force, with the day it applies from.
Open an earlier or upcoming version from the list of versions at the end.
Switch to the English text when you read a translation.
tips: It's part of the terms.
Only the English text is binding; a PDF copy is on the legal docs page.

unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe
unsubscribe.text: Stop one kind of email from testee, or every email from one company, as named on the page.
actions: Read which emails the link stops.
Confirm to unsubscribe; opening the link alone changes nothing.
Signed in, open your email settings afterwards to change other emails.
tips: Service emails, such as team invites, reports and billing problems, still go out; a link that stops a company's emails also stops its invites to you.
